Figured I'd give it a review after just about beating the campaign and spending several hours in the multiplayer, 'cause I do like this game quite a lot.
Pro's:
+ Simple Gameplay, Easy to pick up and be effective while having some more advanced tricks you can pull off.
+ Nice Pixel Work
+ Some actually pretty funny dialouge from the NPC's.
+ Good Music, could use a bit more variety but overall solid and fitting. (Wish we had a vocal Darren Korb track though instead of just instrumental)
+ Pick up and Play matches, only last about 10-15 minutes.
+ Random maps make each game different, yet you have the ability to enter in seeds if you wish to play a certain map.
+ Enjoyable Setting
+ Simple Lobbies, no hassle to play with friends. Cross play coming soon too between GoG and Ps4 Players at different dates.
+ Very open developers with updates on what they are working on.
+ Very Controller Friendly RTS that dosen't subtract the quality of the Mouse and Keyboard and both are even due to the simplicity.
+ Hoppers positive attitude is infectious
Con's:
- The Random Maps. Wait, Didn't I say that was good? Yeah, this one is kind of a double edged sword. Sometimes it's great, sometimes it isn't.
- Campaign is "difficult". Not "hard", but "difficult" since, as mentioned above sometimes you are at the mercy of the map generation, especially if you wish to be a completionist and get the Heroic Objectives. I'd say overall there's about 4 missions that this is criminally accurate to attribute to them.
- P2P Connection means that if one player has a bad connection it can cause slow down for everyone. Unfortunately this is difficult to handle so I can't fault the game too much, it's just a bit of a bother.
- Ranked mode also has random map generation, usually this is fine but it uses the 1 win = 1 Star, 1 loss = -1 star system. This means that if you are unlucky with map generations too bad.
Overall, an enjoyable RTS that is definetly worth the asking price, and I'd jump to recommend to anyone should it go in sale in the future who has an interest in the genre, maybe even if they don't.

Wow - what a refreshing change of pace.
Tooth and Tail is a brilliantly executed spin on the RTS genre. I'm not sure anything with this vision has been made before.
Instead of demanding 150 APM to be played effectively, Tooth and Tail values nuance, strategy, decision-making and micro that is more complex than first appears. To be clear, I'm going to primarily review the multiplayer, although the campaign is great. The campaign is a decent length, a good story, laugh-out-loud funny and impressively challenging.
You control a Commander, that moves with WASD or the stick on your controller. You have access to up to six units, of varying 'tiers' and base defenses. You pick these anew every time you play, so you can experiment as much as possible.
Each player starts with a Gristmill and four farms - out of a maximum eight per mill. They run dry after five minutes, which contributes to the fast-paced gameplay. Most matches are under ten minutes.
It's a race to scout the map and choose your strategy on the fly - each game, the map is randomly generated.
You overwhelm your opponent with a combination of micro, decision-making, and planning. As you play, you develop a feel for economic timings, for whether or not your army can overcome your opponents, as well as understand new micro opportunities.
This game has only just come out, and the playerbase is small, but the developers are imminently going to patch crossplay with PS4 and GoG players, which will add to the multiplayer base.
This game isn't going to replace StarCraft, but it does deserve it's place in the genre and is well-worth picking up if you enjoy RTS's and having a go at. The ladder is forgiving, each game is over quickly so losses don't burn. This game is easy to learn, hard to master.
I highly recommend giving Tooth and Tail a try. It is worth the price.

I am an old school gamer, I do not care if the game has a extremely good graphics or extremely complicated systems. I like things that work good together and tell a somewhat good and enjoyable story.
------------
Here are a few Pro and Con but you must play this game :)
------------
PRO
- Combat System - The best combat system i've seen in years. It's enjoyable and extremely fun. You can fight the monsters with different styles, effects, strategies, etc.
- A.I. - A very good A.I. that fights you in very different ways: wolves surround you and attack in packs, archers run away and hide sometimes, goblins or whatever they are attack in 2 man cells or hide and surprise you and all of them are immune or week to something or you can do something to them to deal more damage, like cutting the reptiles' tails or set the zombie on fire.
- Open World - A good open world with a lot of things to do: main quests, side quests, exploring and others.
- Characters & Party - Many options on how you want your main character and your secondary to be (called pawn here and can be customized almost as the main one), from class to equipment, looks, personality, etc., and you can switch between classes, skills, etc., with each of them. This ads a tactical and strategic layer on top of the combat system. Another thing is that you can have another 2 pawns with you, so a team a 4. The best thing is that they are intelligent and they really help you to find things, quests or they tell and show you how to fight the monsters. They do their own thing so you do not have to control all of them, just your main. It really works good.
- Boss Battles - They are epic. You need to play this game to experience it :). I did not play any other game with this kind of intense fighting.
- Battles - The most enjoyable fights, quests or no quests, i played in years.
------------
CON (not really CON but those are the things that i liked less than the others or i expected a little more from them):
- Graphics - Not the most beautiful game in 2017 but when you fight a 200 meters dragon, in the sky, trying to climb it and cut his throat, I do not think you gonna give a s*** on what texture had the wall you've passed 5 minutes ago, just my opinion (GAMEPLAY OVER GRAPHICS), but even so, the graphics are acceptable.
- UI - Good for old hardcore gamers and rpg gamers, not so good for newcomers. It's made for console and it is a little hard to navigate.
- Quests - Standard quest types but more enjoyable. I expected a little more.
- Voice & Audio - Not very good and not very bad. It's acceptable.
- Story - A simple story that works ok in this game. Don't expect an over complicated one but there are a few enjoyable surprises.
------------
Overall this is a game that concentrates more on the gameplay part and it's doing a great job, combining the monster climbing / fighting from Shadow of the Colossus with Skyrim and a little Dark Souls in some parts. IT'S REALLY A GREAT GAME -> TRY IT!

Ever played Mafia with your friends? This is just like that but better. Every role is interesting in some way, the meta is both well thought out and useful for both sides once you learn how to play, and every round is interesting, even when you die. I'm still learning all the roles and I'm having a blast. Make sure you join the Discord group as it makes it easier to play, though the games population is skyrocketing. Get amongst it!

They're calling this a "social deception" game -- like Mafia which I had watched on some streaming events.  The game's all multiplayer and all about trust and calculated risk.  Even if you aren't an elite multiplayer gamer, as long as you can type and either see through BS or spin BS of your own, you can have fun with this game.  Player base is large enough that games are quickly found and it's also aggressively policing abusive players.  I got this game a week ago but have been really addicted and never had an angry or bad experience so far.
For the game itself -- Generally you have 16 players, 2 starting as an evil faction that always knows who they are and want to kill or take over the good guys, 8-10 on a good faction that start out clueless, with the remainder being neutral with different goals.
There's 2 phases of the game, during the night a lot of action happens -- people get killed, people change factions, people spy on each other.  During the day everyone can talk about what happened, and if they choose they can put anyone else up for an execution vote... if enough join in, there is a trial where the person explains themself and finally everyone votes again whether to kill them or not.
There's different good roles that can you can start with, and each of the 2 evil factions have variations of the good classes.  For neutrals, they have 6 roles with powers that depend on their objectives.
Some roles have killing powers, some can investigate and determine what type someone else is, there are communication classes that can talk to dead players or send anonymous/secret messages, and defensive classes that block many different things.
So the good side doesn't know who's who, but they want to gather lots of info with abilities and figure out how to share it... without revealing to the evil side whether they are good instead of neutral.  If the good side can figure out the evils, then they can easily vote them off.  The game is endless bluffing, literally everyone wants to be seen as allied with the good side, so you dealing in lies and liars from start to finish!

The first thing I thought when playing this game, was it's similarity to the popuar game Town of Salem. However, if you dislike Town of Salem, don't let that turn you away from this game. The classes and factions are also much better balanced, and classes themselves are more fun to play. Instead of having only a few classes that you hope for, you can have fun playing just about every class. There are a couple of classes I personally feel don't have much impact, but the game is constantly improving, so.
The best thing about this game, is that the most important factor is most definitely the players skill. This is a game of deception and logic, and those skills are highly valuable in this game. If you are a good player, you can easily win any game if you're careful. It takes a while to get the hang of a few things, but once you do, you will have some of the most satisfying wins and comebacks.
I honestly just can't wait for there to be a larger playerbase. At any given time, there's around 300-600 people playing. This imeans there's probably 2000 active players. This is enough for you to not have any trouble finding a match quickly, but if there were more then they could start implementing a ranking system. Normally people who play games like this are competitive, so I think it would be a nice addition.

Zombies are currently shambling along in the markets when it comes to gaming. Between titles such as Call of Duty and their Nazi Zombies, Dead Island, Left 4 Dead and a number of others, they had saturated the ground with generic shooting and running to certain checkpoints or just general mayhem which is all good and fun. They still felt lacking however and State of Decay seems to have looked toward what regular people would do in the event of the zombie apocalypse.
Hoarding resources, fragile negotiatons with other survivors/the law/the military, the loss of a valuable team member for good, illnesses in characters that affect their abilities, etc. It's refreshing to have to this view on the end of the world and have to plan out at times what the best course of action for your community is. It still holds enough of running and gunning to have the appeal to a large audience and the actions sometimes caused can be a comedy goldmine. Hitting a feral zombie with the door of your sports car as it attempts to dodge out of the way, only to get nailed dead center and cartwheel through the air for about ten seconds? Priceless.
State of Decay isn't without its negatives however. The first and foremost is the lack of multiplayer of any sort. What fun is beating down zombies if you can't do so with a friend? Reports state that multi was to be implemented, but there was legal issues and the like, so it was overlooked in favor of DLC for the time being and eventually shelved indefinitely. Undead Labs have also issued statements that the next game would focus much more on the multiplayer but there is no specific date set to this sequel and in the meantime, we are all left hanging. Minor negative points also include odd collision detection where a swing will miss point blank and allow your jugular to get a nibble and cars being made of balsa wood and tissue paper in terms of being able to mow down handfuls zombies before bursting into flames.
All in all, the game is fun and can be addictive, looking for those last few materials to build up your workshop to make silencers or a medical area to make sure that favorite character can keep on fighting after a nasty encounter with a freakishly powerful zombie. In terms of numerical value, I'd give it an eight out of ten and recommend any fans of the genre to give this one a try.

My Experience so far.
Ran into a mutant on day one. Killed it, but I was wounded and bled out and died.
Respawned. Avoided mutants and gathered lots of gear. Fell off cliff and died.
Respawned. Gather gear and avoided mutants. Ran into a pack of wolves. Hard fight, but neither side lost. Wolves went on their way. I bandaged up and camped out in an abandon house and logged off for the night.
Logged back on the next day. Exploring and gathering. Learned how to make bandages. Found 12 gauge shotgun. Stumbled into a town. Found an old bus. Started gathering parts to repair. Noticed some parts were being repaired while I was off gathering.
Turns out another player was also repairing the bus. He had to also realise I was repairing it as well for the same reasons. Went into stalk mode. Followed him around without him knowing. Got dark. Set up camp in emtpy office building near the bus to await morning and watch the bus. After a long period the guy never came back. At sun up I decided to gather as many parts as I could carry from the bus and leave him to it.
While doing so, I hear him speak. I freaked! Gun up! Frantic search down the barrel for the source! Nothing. I Ran. I hid. I waited and waited. I concluded I must have heard something else. A glitch maybe?
Went back to bus. Started gathering parts. Two gunshots ring out and almost hit me. I arm my shotgun and run around the building and right into him! He has an assault rifle! Six more shots fire, hitting me a couple of times. I get off four shots, point blank, on him with my shotgun. Dropping him on the spot. I am bleeding bad. My one bandage has no affect. I go to his body hoping he has medical supplies. I die inches from him.
Respawn. I am in a neighborhood. Start the grind of house to house searches. It's raining hard. Thunder and lighting totally drown out all sounds. I start getting paranoid. I scout out the windows of each house before I leave, just to make sure. Sure enough, See guy on roof of gas station around the corner. I stay clear of the window and lean to peek at him. He is looking for something...or someone. I have just respawned and have no weapons. He eventually leaves. Stalk mode back on.
I follow him to the next town. I am scared and unarmed. At least he kills all the mutants in his path. So I am safe from them for now. While following him, he stops and changes directions. Back towards me! I jump into an old beat up van to hide. Guess what is inside? An AK-Freakin-47 with ten rounds in a magazine! I just grew some balls!
I stalk with confidence now. I follow him to the edge of town. Where he meets up with his two friends. Scared again.
I follow this group down the highway, staying in bushes, to the next town. I think they are aware of me now. One of them keeps stopping and looking behind him. I climb on top of a Quickie Mart to monitor them. He runs straight to it. OK. This is it. Lock and load. It's show time! Do or die!
I post up. If he comes up that ladder, I am dropping him. He stops in the middle of the street, turns and rejoins group. They move on. A storm is coming and it is getting darker and the fog is setting in. I have lost track of them. I have to log off for real life. I hide in an old house. I know if I log off I will forever lose them. At least I am packing heat when I log back on.
10/10. Would Stalk again.

OK... given my playtime now, I think it's finally time for my review. No plot spoilers. A proper review would take a look at all aspects, but I don't have much time so I'll be brief.
The game itself is surprisingly good. Of course... it's no Chaos Theory, but regardless, the
. By playing on perfectionist, the game's hardest difficulty, you'll find yourself hiding and waiting a lot; examining the guards' patrol routes (which by the way change every few deaths to keep you on your toes). Also you won't be able to use your vision through walls, giving (albeit briefly) you that similar experience in Chaos Theory when you find yourself constantly wondering what's around the corner.
So what else is there? A diverse array of gadgets, guns and accompanying upgrades for starters. I loved being able to use the money earned from missions to upgrades and improve my loadouts. There was a chain of progression, and I could feel my character becoming a 'stronger' spy, equipped with more stuff as the game continued.
The environments are pretty damn awesome. Exploration is the key to achieving your preferred playstyle. There are neat cinematic scenes and unique parts of the story which require you to play out these almost 'mini-game'-like bits; but they're so well integrated into the story and allows you to take a break from all the running, jumping and stabbing.
Now let's switch over to the multiplayer. There's not much to say about coop. It's essentially singleplayer but with a partner. There is a fairly wide variety of missions to choose from. Each of the main characters have varying game modes depending on what you're up for. Nearly all of them can be played solo if you don't have anyone to trust your life with.
Grab a mic, join your friend, and off you go. That's right. A mic. Whilst not completely essential- it will drastically reduce the number of times you die because of silly mistakes. Bouncing information between you and your partner will really help. But... if you're with a random person you might not be able to do that. In which case, you'll just have to grit your teeth and go with the flow.
Spies. Versus. Mercs. It's fun. Believe it or not, it's actually fun. With friends. By yourself... yeah, I'll admit, you can have some pretty decent matches. But seriously, for some laughs and a better chance at winning- play with friends you can talk to. Skype, TeamSpeak- it's all about information exchange. You can better anticipate that ambush if your buddy just saw a spy heading your way. You can let your friends know where the hacker is by utilising the merc cameras whilst your dead.
The SVM loadouts are different to the singleplayer loadouts, so be prepared to start paying up the big bucks again. This time you'll also need SVM tokens, which allow you to purchase weapons and stuff. You only get a few when you start levelling up and then one token each level after that, so spend wisely. There should be enough to unlock everything, but it's the order you choose that matters. I'll be writing or recording an updated SVM tutorial sometime in the future, to help the new players with how everything works. You'll have fun creating custom loadouts with a combination of gadgets, gear and weapons to your liking and playstyle. The torso abilities are pretty cool. Each side (mercs, spies) get three choices of abilities to aid your plight. Used wisely, you can be a valuable asset to your team.
Since Blacklist is 4 vs 4, it's the perfect number. Every player counts, and when your team mates goes down, you best be prepared for what happens next.
On the face of it though, SVM is fun to dive into for a quick match (I say quick match, it's about 25 - 30 minutes per match). You can just join and start playing straight away. It's fast paced and will require some level of awareness and reflex reactions in order for you to survive. Playing smart is a key skill. Anticipating enemies, knowing your way around the map, always paying attention to the little things that might give away the position of a spy. Classic, Blacklist and Team Deathmatch are probably the only active game modes at the moment. The others could do with a reboot, as they're fun to play... when there's enough players.
I honestly can't really fault the singleplayer. There is one thing though. It can be very easy to speedrun. Grab one of the sniper rifles and just headshoot everyone. Job done. Of course, some armored enemies require a little melee time, but with two or three shots you can drop them just as easily. It can ruin the fun, but it's completely feasible.
Oh, there's also the whole Michael Ironside thing. Yes, Fisher does appear younger. No, it won't stop you from enjoying the game. You'll get used to it. Or perhaps not. It's really up to you.
My negative points reside mostly with the game launcher rather the game itself. Ubisoft only had to go and slap Uplay on its products AGAIN. Why even bother releasing this on Steam if it was going to need Uplay anyway?! For example. I load Uplay (ugh, I know) and click 'Play' on Blacklist. It then says... 'loading Steam. Please wait for your game to load from there'. Like... wut. Then Steam launches Blacklist, then it goes BACK to Uplay and Blacklist opens up. ???
Not only the Uplay interface a pain to reach on a laptop (since it's Shift + F2 and laptop users have to press FN as well...) but it's slow as hell and actually caused me to crash Blacklist once.
Ugh.
Here we go. I'm leaving coop out of this by the way.
Spies vs. Mercs feels like another company developed it and just slapped it onto the main game. Seriously. The sonar vision is completely different to the sonar vision in singleplayer, the way the stun crossbow works is different, there's no crouch sprint... the list goes on. When I first started playing, I got bugs. I mean... BUGS. One particularly game breaking bug was the fact that every time I went into cover and left it, I'd stand up and start sprinting around. It was hella annoying. Ubisoft put out THREE patches and none of them fixed it. It was only after I'd posted a couple ideas and experiments of the forums that someone else picked it up and fixed it. A fix, from the community ._.
If you're buying Blacklist for the SVM, wait for a deal. SVM, in its current state, is just not worth it. Overrun with hackers and the likes, SVM has become a tense community, filled with paranoid players who don't trust each other. And why should they? With Ubisoft turning their back on the game, with no dedicated servers (Host changed. Migrating match.) and no anti-cheat system, you have no idea who could be hacking, or who's just damn lucky. Tired of the hackers? Want to quit the match? Tough. Ubisoft removed the Quit Match button to 'reduce the number of unfair rage quitters'. Uhm, wut.
Seriously, all the more reason to team up with people you trust and can communicate with. You can still beat hackers, because they're dumb. They can whiz around and kill you with one bullet, but they're idiots who can still be killed with Death From Above and unexpected melees. Even hackers bleed.
Conviction was fun, but Blacklist brings more to the table. With new ways to play, and new gadgets to play with, the singeplayer and coop are definitely a must. Just watch out for the SVM, it might not be what you were completely expecting.

is a hard game to describe. It’s weird, strange, interesting, odd, confusing, quirky.
It’s also damned fun. A rather short experience at just over 2.5 hours (longer if it takes you more time to figure out some of the puzzles), but in that 150 minute timespan, you’re treated to an interesting story with a really weird but intriguing cast of characters, great level design, and fantastic music.
You play as a guest arriving at The Norwood, a weird hotel that’s known for being the home of a musician, Peter Norwood, way back. The man was as eccentric as the people you encounter and need to help out. A group of musicians working on new material, an employee who loves Blue Moose, front desk clerks who are coy about things in the hotel, and many more.
The game centers around you completing tasks for the various guests, to unlock access to locations that help you collect items to be able to talk to a DJ, which is the ultimate goal in the game. All the characters have unique dialogue when you’ll overhear, and they change what they say as you get closer when they address you directly. Some of the tasks you need to do can be confusing, but there’s a front desk concierge who can point you in the right direction.
It’s a very pretty game to look at, filled with weird and macabre decorations, twisting hallways, odd rooms, and more surreal things. It’s accompanied by a fantastic soundtrack that really immerses you into the game.
All in all,
is an excellent adventure game. You won’t rack your brain on its simplistic puzzles, but you’ll enjoy the atmosphere and story of this twisted and surreal world.

-Spell use - limited by number of casts between sleeps (meaning you better carry tons of firewood) .  Reminds me of C&C 4 and the depature from typical RTS.  Just makes the game un enjoyable. Some say they do this to make it more challenging and or casters are too powerful. I personaly would rather see less dmg on a caster with the ability for me to actually cast without having to rest.  Never knew micromanagement could be done in an RPG - these programmers found a way for that.
- Gone with the Wind type texts for everything.   Overwelming amount of texts for the most simple things.
Way overly compliacted.  You have 5 main upgrade choices on levels. Lore Scroll reading, Survival (consumable duration), Stealth,, Mechanics (lock picking), and Athletics.
Typical RPG's use INT / STR / DEX / CON etc where you apply points into these when leveling - not here.  I only found gear could upgrade those and very modestly.
Items / Gear upgrades are very anti - exciting as you realize that any low level item can be "enchanted" to Exceptional / Superb which is the same as the drops you get from bosses - making the boss drops nothing special.
Endurance is now part of the equation similar to "health" - when your endurance hits zero you pass out (in a fight) but your health doesn't improve.  There is no healing or health potions - just endurance.  But you can die apprently if your health goes to zero. Not sure why not just sticking to basic Hitpoints was a bad thing.
MOBS you kill give you virtually no xp - experience gain is mainly quest driven. The items dropped are just an overabundance of useless items maybe for potions or vendor trash.
One aspect I liked was owning a "stronghold" so you can rest there and get bonus'.  Initially it was great until you realize it's nightmare always attenidng to "unwanted visitors" that you have to pay off to not stay (it brings negative prestige) or escort and are constantly getting invaded that I have to go back to the stronghold (2 days travel) to fight.  You can have it auto resolve by hiring defenders that get paid but that means you can take damage to your stronghold.  Good idea that turned into more micromanagement.
Some may like this unobvious level of micromanagement throughout the game- but I hated it.  I will almost guarantee most any person that plays this game will saving every few minutes if that gives an indicator of frustration.    The dragon fights (possible 3)  - I never got through any of them - not even close to defeating one (i was level 12 the max level).
The main battle at the end same thing.  I got to the end - but game so frustating - uninstalled the game with only 1 boss to kill at the end.

This is the best RPG I have played in a VERY long time. Deep deep lore, great character, amazing story, fantastic combat. Seriously, whats not to like? Be warned, there is a learning curve (plenty of guides out there though) and you should be prepared to give up your life and livelyhood (I'm 44 hours in and feel I've barely scratched the surface).
Ok, time to head back in! Enjoy!

Character Classes:
There is a massive imbalance between the powers of various classes.  If you like playing a spellcaster, then you will probably hate this game because of the bizarre and excessive limitations placed on their spell casting.  If you like playing an Archer, then you may be disappointed because you are stuck with a weak pet, and when that pet (quickly) dies, you will be stuck doing wimpy damage.  The melee classes are all pretty strong, and they added a strange new type of melee-spellcaster that trumps all of the magic users combined.   It's almost like the devs hated magic users, but begrudgingly allowed one halfway decent class that is "magic but isn't magic" for marketing purposes.   In any case, this is NOT a pick-whatever-class-you-want kind of game.  If you play at the highest difficulty levels, you pretty much are forced to play a fighter of some sort.
Gamplay:
What gameplay?   Most of what you do is auto-attack and waiting for the right moment to use one-shot special abilities.  If you want more excitment, go play bridge or bingo.   This game is all about cooldowns, restrictions, and auto attack.  Once you (very) quickly run out of spells, you will literally be hitting mobs with a book.  Yeah that is about as fun and effective as it sounds.  There is no real strategy involved,  Just smash things before they smash you, and try not to run out of camping gear and spells before the end of a dungeon.
Story:
The writing is a bit broody and melodramatic, and really a rehash of every fantasy concept ever written.  If it were a novel, I would be embarrased to have it in my collection.  It was not even compelling enough to make it to the middle, let alone the end.
Dialog:
This is actually the best part of the game.  Almost immersive.  Really if you like reading dialog, you might enjoy this game.   But you have to have a high tolerance for all the other snooze-inducing faults of the game.
Conclusion:
If you loved Balders Gate, but thought the combat didn't impose enough arbitary cooldowns and resitrictions, then you will love this game.

Being a part of the Steam launch community, tracking the Ur-Dragon's health on Reddit, and discussing builds and tactics in the early days were my favorite things about this game. Since the release-rush to murder Ur is over, online interaction with others is minimal at this point. You can still fight and kill Ur online with the help of others, but it won't be as lively as it was at launch.
As a single-player adventure, I still recommend it to those looking for a new combat system to learn, a large world to climb and explore, and unique, punishing enemies. This game has a very steep learning curve. A lot of bad reviews come out of the grind of the early game, before advance professions and before you get the chance to come back through and easily stomp those goblins that gave you too much trouble.
This game rewards persistance and exploration. Not just map exploration, but mechanics exploration as well. Often times, you'll feel like you're throwing yourself at a wall, only to realize that there was a much easier way of dealing with that mob or dungeon.
For me, this game scratches a lot of itches, but not all at once. There are times you blow up hordes of rouges with a meteor storm. There are times you're spamming blast arrows with Tenfold Flurry. Times you gotta solve puzzles underground. Times you gotta sneak around gaurd patrols. There are large cities to climb and explore for hidden shops and hidden chests. I spent over an hour climbing around the first town before setting foot outside and fighting the first goblin.
And then there's times you're yelling at your AI pawns to do the one thing you recruited them for and all they do is say, "THEY ARE WEAK TO FIRE!" and then enchant your weapons with frost. Be prepared to hear the same voice lines time and time again. Be prepared to watch your pawns needlessly sacrafice themselves to trolls. I've gotten so frustrated, I picked them up one by one and threw them off a cliff into the sea. I'm glad you can do things like that. I don't feel so bad hitting them with my fire wall when they don't get out of the way.
As frustrating as some mechanics can be, it's just part of Dragon's Dogma's charm. When things go right, it feels awesome. When things go horribly wrong, you're reminded this world IS out to kill you. Mobs don't treat you better than any other NPC just because you're the player character. Most NPCs expect you to die.
TLDR: Dragon's Dogma is it's own game with it's own charm. Steep progression curve. Immersive mechanics. Lots of content. Firey explosions. Large bosses. Stabbing things, a lot. Character creation. Loot. Rusted bow that magically slows down bosses so they float majectically through the air. Etc. Etc.
Prefekt 5/7.

The biggest draw about this game is possibly its biggest turn-off: that it plays exactly like the early 2000 Infinity Engine RPGs that the late 20's-early 30's crowd grew up with.
There are some modern twists thrown in. But at the end of the day, PoE is unapologetically old school. Which may or may not be a bad thing. If you've played any of the Infinity Engine games, you'll be met with little to no learning curve here. The 2D, isometric graphics look beautiful. The gameplay is nuisanced and well-thought out.
For the most part, it's exactly what you'll expect from its subgenre. It certainly won't win any awards for innovation, but it accomplished what it set out to do very well.
Unfortunately being old school also means it doesn't take many chances. Fantasy roleplaying has moved on from the early 2000s' sensitivities. Audience today are used to darker, more edgy stuff. Compared to other dark fantasy franchises like Dragon Age or Divinity. PoE's adventure failed to reach the social relevance and/or emotional impact of its 2 main competitors.
Perhaps my biggest complaint though is the plethora of bugs - also a staple of oldschool RPGs. Some of the bugs encountered are downright gamebreaking. We're 6 months into release and they show no sign of being cleaned up for good.
The biggest reason for me to recommend this as a must-buy though, it's the fact that it is obviously a labor of love. And as a new IP it still has plenty of room to grow and improve. I certainly hope the franchise has a long and prosperous future, where I can waste hundreds of hours on.

The use of weapons is very realistic. Blocking and countering attacks, using Judo and maybe a little jujitsu from what little I can recognize using real world experience. Katana's, wakizashi’s, tanto's, spears and of course your bare hands to defeat enemies is fun to say the least. Hopefully way of the Samurai 5 will have archery and ridable horses.
You can pick your character’s face and outfit to start and after you unlock more of the game hair color, sex, skin color, and Hight too. Unfortunately, there does not appear to be a sumo body to pick from.
It’s easy to get confused if you are new to the Way of the Samurai game series. Just remember every action has a reaction and affects your end story line. There are several different endings. If you do different things and get the same ending each time, try doing missions for a different group entirely. Or a Single group throughout the game. The is no wrong ending just different ending based on your actions as well as the things you say. Choose carefully or you are likely to get the same ending over and over. The most common ending is the easiest to get and you will probably get it the first few times. You will know this ending because you will hate it. That ending makes you hate a certain character whom you want to take actions against which will often give you that exact same ending. Tring not to give you a spoiler but don’t always do the most obvious or more likely the easiest thing. It’s okay to go a little nuts on an individual if you are prepared to fight them there for removing that ending or part of the end game.

+It has a world with a diverse array of events and endings where the choices you make matter. Some of the events feel so coincidential they almost have to be googled, which can be good or bad, but simply put, there's a lot to explore.
+The story can be generic with a sort of "go here, do this", but the characters have human passions and beliefs though they act silly (the silliness can also be a boon as it's often amusing).

-The combat has blocking, dodging, combos, and so on, but it's all too simple to find and repeat a combo to keep your enemy staggered, so it can be repetitive.
-The PC port has a few bugs for me, nothing too troublesome. You need a controller as there's no mouse support.
-Allegedly they promised DLC and failed to deliver.
-Swords are based on a shallow system where only damage is worth much consideration.
-Crafting is grindy, involving hours to get certain charms or inscription (max of each, anyways). Again, damage is the primarily important stat, at least for beating the campaign, and there is no multiplayer.
Choosing between yes and no really tears me apart, but I opt for yes in subjectivity. I didn't particularly mind the repetition because of the many styles. I actually enjoy grinding to a limited extent after doing much more in MMOs. The bugs were extremely minor for me, and I already own a controller, so no harm done there. The swords complaint is relatively insignificant. The only thing I'm somewhat salty about is the DLC, but then, I can't even find any online evidence of reviewers' claims.

This game has reaffirmed my love for PC gaming.  The game is fun, frentic, and in some cases outright terrifying.  I can't count the number of times I was scavenging goods assuming I was safe when suddenly a Feral zombie ripped my survivor to shreds.  Or, the times I was fighting a small group of zombies to level up my skills when the tides turned an a hoard of zombies overtook my charatcer and killed them.  And if your character dies they're gone for good.  This game forces you to think and plan ahead each and every time you venture out into the game world to run a mission, search for goods, or simply try to keep the undead at bay.  In this regard State of Decay is exactly the zombie game you want to play.
Not all that glitters is gold however.  The combat is clunky and some animations are poorly executed.  On the PC the game looks much better than its XBOX 360 counterpart, but even with the new sheen applied the game is overall relatively ugly and looks very much like a first release for the last generation of consoles.  Don't let this stop you from buying the game though!  Even with the somewhat bland graphics the game is simply fun to play.  You'll find your heart racing out of fear rather than the outdated graphics causing palpatations.  The voice acting is cringe inducing and the character development in terms of story telling and narrative is laughable.  The story itself is very poorly delivered and you'll find yourself caring less about the story and more about the action as you travel between one plot element to the next.  And the game is also relatively short if you devote a few hours to following the story elements only.
Even with its shortfalls State of Decay is a must play game.  You'll find no other game quite like it to slate your zombie survival thirst.  Hopefully the developers will continue to support the game with additional content and here's hoping to a sequel!

In many ways this is the beginnings of the zombie game I have been waiting for. A zombie survival game with an "end game" - survivor communities.
As it stands I enjoyed what State of Decay offers, but perhaps I have enjoyed it more as a proof of concept than anything else. The world of State of Decay is well realised, and the scale is spot on - the map is full of various points of interest without being too cluttered. The story elements are decent enough as you are guided through the game world - although you do have to fill in a lot of the blanks yourself.
There is a lot missing, most notably human enemies / survivor wars - one group in particular I swear was leading up to this... nope. Why am I watching a zombie climb over a barbed wire fence? Hmm. There are some oddities found throughout the game like this.
Beyond the survivor communities mechanic, vehicles add a joyous experience to the "zombie murdering" genre (if I can call it that). State of Decay's animations are mostly great (if jerky at times) and the graphics, while dated, are charming. The way zombies move and you combat them is much better realised here than in other zombie survival games. Melee combat is nicely played too.
All in all I recommend this game, if only to support Undead Labs' future work. If State of Decay is any indication, we're in good hands.
UPDATE: Lifeline DLC was quite fun - great to get a new map to explore, and a few new characters. Definitely worth a few dollars if you'd like to journey back into the world of State of Decay. Some welcome enhancements, too: vehicle storage and automatic unloading of supplies are awesome.

Nominated for the "Just 5 more minutes" award.
What can I say? The whole game is based around just five more minutes. Whether it's just five more minutes until I get back to the boss, just five more minutes until I get to the next bonfire checkpoint, or just five more minutes(hours) until I give up.
Dark souls is both a challenging and methodical approach to the modern day dungeon crawler, and plays similar to an action RPG. Areas are intricately crafted with beautiful scenery, and every enemy and item has a purpose and reason for being there. So whether it's because you decided to walk the wrong direction at Firelink Shrine or maybe dealing with the archers of Anor Londo, there's always something there to make you hate yourself a bit more in this game, just because you know that the mistakes are all on you. The 'Open' world is also a nice change of pace from its PS3 predecessor Demon Souls, and feels atmospherically better than its sequel, Dark Souls II, despite a several flaws such as a 30fps lock.
There are many who enjoy a challenge, but even more who are turned off by it. However, with some effort and habit breaking, even an unexperienced gamer would be able to enjoy this game. The game has gone on sale as low as 5 USD, but it is well worth the full 20 USD price.

Wow, impressive. Chucklefish really did it. They took a game with a lot of potential and hype behind it, made it pretty average and left it in EA to rot seemingly forever. But then, against all odds, against what all the experts were saying, they really turned it around AND MADE IT ♥♥♥♥ING WORSE.
I'm just baffled. Just how awful of a developer do you have to be to do this to your procedurally generated space-exploration game. Just how cruel?
Let me tell you the sad story of Starbound.
This game went through a lot of stages in it's long, VERY LONG Early Access phase (3 years.). And impressively, it just kept getting worse and worse with every update! Originally it was a simple randomly generated space-exploration game, with a lot of potential and possibility. You started off in your ship as one of a few races, an exile of that race, with your own unique backstory and an enormous potential for a brilliant personal story in the future. As an Avian for example, you were an Atheist, running from your species of religious zealots who murdered your loved one because of a ritual involving a black feather. You started off with a few books explaining your personal story, and that was it. I hoped only for now.
After that point, the universe was open to you. Every single planet you landed on had randomly generated enemies, at first very cheap looking ones with boring abilities, but they were improved in the first few updates (The good few updates) to both look more interesting and match their envioroment. You potentially had desert spiders spewing fire, snow ghosts with teleportation abilities, volcano heads, cyborgs. It gave you the feeling that every single planet was unique, having it's own animal life and whenever you landed on of them it was simply fun to run around it's surface and see what types of animals were generated this time. Later, you would have randomly generated mini bosses, and an unbelievable amount of weapons (Rivaling Borderlands).
You had instructions for the first boss in a book, a penguin spaceship which you summoned to the surface. The boss was good fun and you could make use of the the surface of the planet both to your adventage and determent. After killing the first boss, you went on to new planets, you had an enormous universe, filled with various types of planets and hundreds of hours of potential gameplay. Snow planets, volcano planets, tentacles, arid, ocean, jungle, radioactive, tentacles, you name it. Every single one of them having different weapons, ores and enemies. It was, safe to say, pretty decent. But would get very boring rather fast, with the game eventually falling apart into you just mining ore for hours.
So what did Chucklefish do with this? Did they improve on the forumala, add new bosses, more weapons, improve combat, add more planets, better mob generation, new mechanics and create a space-exploration game for the ages? Yes and ♥♥♥♥ NO THEY DIDN'T.
Instead, they just randomly decided to change the entire ♥♥♥♥ing game, screwing everyone over who stuck with them for all these years (Like me, who played every new update, that's why I have a 100 hours.) and turning the entire game into a linear, pre-made abomination. With it's exploration elements still stuck in half-life like an undead beast.
The personal story every race had? GONE! Removed! Instead you're just a random nobody in a dumb galatic federation of all the races that didn't even exist before. The fun bosses with which you could build your own arenas for and decide your own strategy for? GONE! Replaced with incredibly easy bosses in pre-made arenas.
They went on to add a personal AI on your ship who tells you everything you need to do. A ridiculous amount of story moments with NPCs which tell you an unbelievably bad story completely deprived of mystery and excitment. Dull, simple quests to guide you along step-by-step through the entire game.
The biggest sin they commited here is how they changed the enemies in the game. And this is such an unbelieveably bad decision it will be difficult for me to write without going on a huge caps-lock rant. They added hand-made mobs to all the planets, THE SAME ♥♥♥♥ING MOBS, TO ALL THE PLANETS! Not only do they look like complete crap but WHAT THE ♥♥♥♥? This is supposed to be a space-exploration game, we have a UNIVERSE to explore, planets that are HUNDREDS OF LIGH YEARS APART. How do I see the EXACT SAME ♥♥♥♥ing mobs on every single one of those planets?? It's absolutely ridiculous!
Then the new races which they introduced, I swear the developers had a stroke while designing them. Or they just wanted to troll everyone. Let me pull a test here, for the reader. You are a creature designer in a sci-fi game with an enormous universe. You are supposed to design a species that lives on a huge rock floating in the middle of nowhere. What do you design? If your answer was "Idk, an alien of some kind?" then congratulations, you are not completely creatively dead! What did the developers design? A BEAR. A ♥♥♥♥ING BEAR. No, not a space bear, not a rock bear, just a bear. A normal brown bear. That's it folks. That's the type of species you will encounter. IN SPACE.
Others include (And I'm not joking here.) Alpaca, penguins and frogs. Not alien alpaca or penguins or frogs. No, just frogs. Your standard Earth frogs. THAT'S WHAT YOU GET, IN A SCI-FI GAME!
So now you just trudge through this pathetically boring universe, with a pathetically boring story. From one planet to the other, "finding" new ores (Ore you have been told is there, and you have been sent to collect it.) pretending like you are having fun.
It just turned into your average crappy pixel indie story game. Any potential it ever had dead. Do not buy. Unless you really want to interact with Earth bears on other planets.

This game is immersive, beautiful and has next to no performance issues. It also has devs that actively talk with members of the community in hopes of making the game better in any way they can, despite it missing some features, it is a mostly fully functional Zombie Survival/PVP game, it even features wild life that can destroy you (my story below goes into this further), pick this up, play it for however long you want, you can always come back to it a few months later and be greeted with some new content/features. This game can make your heart beat fast, it can make you second-guess your morals. Ammo is usually hard to find but guns can be quite easy to come across if you look in built up areas (towns, the city, heck, even some stores). This is the end of my review, the rest of the "review" will be the story of my first life.
This all took place in my first life, my first time playing the game. I spawned at the edge of a forest, I saw a few houses ahead, it was almost pitch-black, I went ahead and looted them, only finding a hatchet and a few useless pistol mags, I was shining my trusty flashlight in the house, it illuminating the house with me unaware. I heard a guy call out to me, turns out him and his buddy were just some friendly guys in the middle of nowhere with some assualt rifles, I followed them around a bit before we began looting the rest of this small town we ended up in, we walked into the forest for whatever reason and supposedly we were going to the city, so I tagged along, in the very waking hours of the morning, the sun just rising above the treeline we heard howls, it was the
, they began shooting at the wolves, it was a huge pack of them, easily 20 or more of them, I made a ran for it after being told they would hold them back, leaving them behind in hopes they make it out alive, they didn't, I never heard from them again. I was at the edge of the forest now and the sun had risen, I was now inside a large town, not a city but pretty huge. I came across roughly 15-20 people in the town, all looting, everyone was friendly, no one had guns, at least we thought so, I was looting a department store when outside out the corner of my eye I notice a taxi, it wasn't in a condition to drive but it was close enough, all it needed was spark plugs, two wheels, some oil and some fuel. I set out to look for it before coming across 2 people, both of them were friends and completely new to the game like me, so I told them about the car and what we needed and we set out to raid the town of every piece we needed, we managed to find spark plugs, oil and the two wheels but we lacked fuel, we couldn't find it anywhere. Anyway we went back to the car to install the components we had recently found around the town, before having a sit down and talking for about 10 minutes about how we're gonna find fuel and where we could, we were about to head to a nerby "Gas Station" before being stopped by what we thought was a fellow peer, he was on top of the department store, he offered us fuel for some of our clothing, we thought to ourselves, "it's a fair deal, why not!" but before we knew it he shot one of us in the leg, luckily we were already behind the taxi so I made my T-Shirt into a rag and used it as a bandage to stop him from bleeding, after we fixed up his leg we made a run for it, the gunman tried to shoot us as we started our run for safety, we bolted through the department store and ran into a nearby forest, he got a shot in my lower back, I was bleeding heavily, the gun man was still chasing us but he had to climb down off the roof so we were a good 50m ahead of him, next thing we knew, we were in the middle of a forest being amushed by a pack of wolves. We ran away from the town because we would've got shot if we was to head back to the town, so we ran to the other side of the forest, long behold our saviour, a massive water tower that was taller than anything we saw in the town, all 3 of us safely made it up the ladder but I was bleeding hard, luckily I had a spare rag and I stopped my bleeding just in time, I was on 2% HP, on the brink of death. Just as we thought we were safe and we made our way down the ladder, we heard more wrenching growls from the Wolves below, they waited for us to come down (now thats some impressive AI), I can't say how fast we climbed straight back up the ladder. We figured out a plan, 2 of us had axes, me and 1 of the others, I was on 2% HP, I was hungry, thirsty and I don't believe I could make it, I gave the axe to the unarmed one, in true heroic fashion they said to me, "You'll make it threw, we'll make sure of it." Those words have stuck with me since, I watched over them as they climbed down the ladder. I wished them luck and watched some fight off the wolves, I watched my only 2 friends get mauled to death by a pack of wolves, before my eyes, I couldn't take it anymore, I was hungry, thirsty and afraid. I made a decision honour their death and try to make a run for it, it was suicide for sure but if I could make it through, I could live to tell the tale. This is a pretty cool game.  I would rate it a 7-8/10 because it’s still an early access game.  There is still a lot of opportunity for this game as it develops…so I would recommend it.  Even in its present situation it will provide endless hours of fun.  Besides, the chances of dying are realistic…unless you save your game and reload it…
1. If you touch a lionfish or sea urchin, or decide to eat a clownfish…and have no pills to nullify the poison…DEATH.
2. If you fall from too high of a spot and nearly break a leg or possibly do so…and you have no medicine or bandages…DEATH
3. If you get bit by a shark and begin to bleed…and do not have a bandage…DEATH.
4. If you go out at night and swim down too fast or the temp gets too cold…and you do not have enough food and water around to overcome the loss in those two categories…DEATH.
5.  Do not eat or drink (water) enough...DEATH.
Graphics:
Spectacular - sand, water, sky, animals, trees, shrubs, etc.
Sunrises and sunsets are cool.  I try to build my house so it faces those directions.
Weapons and items look really good
Sounds are really good too.  Sharks:  When one gets close...the music kind of makes you nervous.  They can knock you out of your life raft...be careful.  When they drag you down...its makes you think...is that how it would be?  Music played near your death is morbid…but really cool.  Once in a while it plays even when you are doing ok…so, it kind of freaks you out.
Once you get flippers though...they are less of a threat.  You can swim fast and chase them down before they turn on you.  Chop them up and eat them for dinner...DON'T FORGET TO COOK THEM FIRST!
Neat Features:
Dragging items around.  You can drag a shark to shore, pull a tree across the beach, and throw items too.
Building options - lot of options.  You can build a three level hut with a balcony.
Items - many to choose from.
Shipwrecks - searching the wrecks for items.
Lighting - underwater - its hard to see without a flashlight or torch.
DEEP Water - Man that stuff is so deep and dark...i cannot tell which way is up.  AVOID!  Plus, you just might get sickness from it.
Things to improve upon:  DO NOT LET THESE ITEMS KEEP YOU FROM GETTING IT THOUGH:
1. No shadow.  All you see is the shadow of the item in your hand.
2. Has to be a way to get the poisonous clown fish off your spear or out of your net without touching it.  I would fling it off my spear...just saying.
3. Can’t carry many items.  It takes FOREVER to bring wood back to my main beach to continue my housing project.  It gets a little annoying making so many trips.
4. hard to put items near the fire to cook.  Once you put together the cooking tripod around the fire... you can only really cook one thing.
5.  Laggy with items in a massive pile
6. It’s hard to stand items up.  You have to drop your pale of freshwater while looking forward - out onto the horizon.
7.  Nothing floats if it falls into the water...even a coconut, plastic water bottle, sticks, and a plastic paddle oar.
8.  Too many items in your boat and it sinks... a lighter, flare, and a roll of duct tape...it begins to take on water.  Add a piece of cloth...and its going down!
9.  Items in your boat fall out very easily...including you...when a shark rubs your boat.
10.  No way to know what makes what without going online to look for a wiki... which you definitely could not do if your plane crashed and you were on a deserted beach.
11.  Sharks do not return to areas where they have been killed - so far.
12. No footprints.
13.  You have to look at your arm with the watch to see what is wrong with you...bleeding...poisoning...injury... Sounds do help though.  Eventually, you figure it out, but otherwise...it is a little tough.  You do not see blood on the ground if you walk around and bleeding.
13.  Sharks do not get cut when you hit it with an axe or machete.  You hear it being hit, but you are unsure if you are really doing anything...unless you have played it a bit.

Fans of Tex Murphy have waited far too long for an answer to the cliffhanger that Overseer left them with. Tesla Effect does an admirable job of bringing Tex into the 2010s, but this game is strictly for the fans. Newcomers will likely be confused.

Often when old series are revived in modern installments, the gameplay is changed or dumbed down to appeal to modern audiences, leaving fans alienated.  Not so with Tesla Effect. The gameplay is more or less identical to the last few efforts,  for good or ill. While not as fiendishly difficult as Under a Killing Moon or TPD, there are still puzzles to be found sprinkled throughout the game. There are many surprisingly well-acted and high budget, high-resolution FMVs, some great humour and alternate endings depending on some decisions taken. Weaknesses are the length and the way the story seems to fizzle out half way through (many major plot events are simply left hanging).

Nostalgia to the MAX. While I never even heard of Tex Murphy prior to this game, it does make me want to go back and play the older ones. The FMVs are the great, using the advances of the past several years. The 3d graphics are notably dated, reminding me of early 2000 games. But we arent here for the graphics, it would be like playing CoD for the story. The story is excellent, given its goofy/campy nature (which I feel makes it even better, too many games these days try to make themselves to be more serious and profound that they really are). The plot is something right out of the 90s-00s cyperpunk genre. I could rattle on and on about this game, but I wont. So Ill just give it a good thumbs up. If you like cyberpunk, film noir, have about of nostalgia for 90s-00s games and/or point/click adventures. This is a good buy for you.

Well, that was werid. It had me smiling the whole time and there are surprises around every corner. The dialog is very strange, but the game allows you to walk away from conversations whenever you're tired of them. Characters help you feel like a part of the world by looking at you when they speak to you. Everything is a little unsettling without going into horror territory.
The audio is amazing! Every room and every person has their own strange ambient way of tickling your ears. The major plot is about music, so a lot of the game pivots around referencing musical instruments. The way that this game sounds will stick with me for a while.

I play a lot of weird indie games, but this probably takes the cake for absurd surrealism. It's ostensibly an adventure game/walking simulator where you talk to and help the various denizens of the hotel and collect pieces of a costume that will let you into the super rad party in the basement, but the real joy of this game is just exploring the hotel in eager anticipation of whatever utter nonsense will assault your senses next. And it's *wonderful*.

The Norwood Suite is a surreal game set in a vast hotel in the mountains. The atmosphere and soundtrack are unlike anything I've seen, even a bit different from Cosmo D's last title, Off-Peak. The majority of the game is spent reading dialogue and searching for items, but most of the entertainment comes from the exploration factor. You could theoretically complete the game without knowing a single thing about the plot, as this game doesn't force anything down your throat. Instead, the game trusts your intelligence and your ability to actively seek out knowledge within the game's environment. The entire plot is contained within written dialogue and letters that you find strewn about or hidden in drawers.
Througout the game, there is a general dark undertone despite the calm music and casual conversation of the hotel's residents. Something about the world isn't quite right, although exactly what is never quite revealed, leaving you to put the pieces together and come up with your own theories. If you don't like games that do this, fine, don't put 10 bucks down the drain. However, if you like puzzle games in which the only puzzle is figuring out what the hell is going on, this one's going to be one of your faves (it's one of mine).

First of all let me say that Playing this game without a controller is not as fun or as easy to do than with a keyboard. Now that thats out of the way:
Story:
The Story in Way Of The Samurai has many different paths and endings i think there is about 9 total. There are three factions in the game The Japanese Goverment , The Europeon Foreigners , And the Foreigner Hating rebels. You can choose to support one of these factions till the end or switch in between. You do not actually have to any side ad could just fish for all four days the story takes place. The game dosent force you to do any thing and theres plenty of side missions and activities to fill those four days without doing any main missions at all. Some of these side missions and characters you meet can be very strange and some very normal. This game can go from batshit crazy to super serious in a matter of seconds. Which is Sort of what i love about it but not all of you will agree.
Gameplay:
Most of the fun in this game after your first playthrough is trying out all the different styles and collecting the hundreds of swords in this game. maybe not hundreds but there is atleast over 100 different weapons. The different stances and movesets in the styles you unlock and collect can be very different from each other and some are easier than others to use.
The combat is not anything too special really. Pretty standard blocking and attacking except for the spring harvest mode which lets you rip through everyone or atleast to tons of damage on harder difficulties. You can carry 10 items with you but using them during combat is not too great of an idea cause it leaves you open to attacks.
Final Verdict:
The Sword Collecting and Trying out different styles has to be my favortie part of this game.As well as any changes you make to the game world during a story or side mission carries on in newgame+ . Getting all the story paths can be frustrating but should provide you with plenty of hours of entertainment. The controls might take a bit to get used to but after an hour or so of play you get used to it. look up gameplay to see if this is the game for you cause it certainly isnt for everyone.

I used to play hours and hours of the original mafia party game through my mid teens. Always been a fan of those kinds of games. Then I played the♥♥♥♥♥♥out of Epic Mafia, both with randoms and with the occasional massive /v/ room.
There are many versions of it to play online too, like Epic Mafia and Town of Salem, but I have to say, this one is by far the most polished and engaging one.
First of all, the two current gamemodes have some focus on a mechanic of conversion. Anybody who proves to be a good guy might not STAY a good guy. It's really hard to trust anyone with that in mind, because if you do, it probably will come back to bite you.
Second of all, every role has many abilities to use during the day and/or night. You're never at the mercy of waiting or unable to do anything. Smart use of abilities and just the right amount of luck can turn games around, or completely ruin them. That does mean the learning curve is a bit higher, even if the motions are generally the same, but the game has a built-in guide that lets you see all the classes any time and a wiki that's kept tidy by the ever growing community.
In other words, if you like the mafia/werewolf kinda game of deception, this is the single best one in the market at the moment, hands down. Definitely check it out.

This is an absolutely stellar port of my favorite of the early Sonic titles. At the price it's going for as I write this, it's a steal. If you're looking for an excuse to pick this title up, here it is.

The main selling point of this game has to be the combat. So few games allow you to climb you enemies and attack them while clinging on; very Shadow of the Colossus. As well as a lot of Monster Hunter type crafting where you'll be hunting down monsters to upgrade your weapons. "They're masterworks all, you can't go wrong." There's also an interesting pawn system where you create your own AI companion which you can customise as much as your main character but have no direct control over. As well as two other pawns created by other players; you can choose from an almost endless list of pawns to use. If you're into fantasy RPG this is a must try, more so with it being on sale so often.
Graphically it's showing it's age. With it originally being a PS3 Xbox 360 game, but the major problems with those versions was the frame rate which would struggle to hit 30 whereas this PC port has been running at a steady 120fps for me. Obviously your performance will vary but it seems to run well for a lot of people.
The story and questing is a bit hit and miss for some people. I've always taken the story as metaphorical, which also means kind of nonsensical at points. You don't really follow much of a story chain just quests that happen to lead you in a direction. So it can be hard to tell if you're progressing or just doing side stuff. You can also progress without meaning to and lock out side quests which is annoying but there's a lot of replayability since you carry your character over into new playthroughs.
It's a large open world which can take some time to get across but you can manually place fast travel points. There are only 2 by default and a max of 10 (I believe.) Which might be a pro or con for a few people. Though there are a lot of hidden locations around the map which can be hard to come by.
There are huge amounts of different gear to choose from. There's an achievement to get something like six or eight hundred different pieces of gear which I didn't get until my fifthed or so play through.
Then you've also got the Dark Arisen which was originally an expansion. It's not very big but it's a fair challenge. I wouldn't attempt it until you've beaten the game at least once or been able to beat the optional end game boss.

A fantastic hybrid of Assasins Creed's traversal and The Batman Arkham series combat set in the lore rich world of LOTR. This game really impresses. While not perfect, much of the action is fluid and interesting.
The story feels very much in line with the novels and films, and could be a hidden missing chapter, though perhaps focused more on a tropey heroic arch as opposed to Tolkiens more 'humble overcomes power' narrative. But it works really well for the game.
The nemesis system is brilliant pitting you against Uruks who have grown stronger by defeating you in battle. Hunting them down and trying to break the  their power structure of the Uruk army is a fun enough system you could just focus on that and be entertained for many hours.
The only major concern I have with the game as a whole is a slightly disjoined feel to the pacing of the story and other elements. Though lore filled, many of the mission structure elements feel sort of bolted on. it doesnt feel like it builds so much as things happen randomly. Sometimes its a quicktime event or a following mission or a big battle with many enemies, but it isnt structured like it had a purpose, and there isnt any tension or sense of you getting closer to an end or climax it just sort of comes to a close.
All in all it is a very solid game and very much enjoyable. If only it had felt more epic overall as all of its parts are perfect to make this happen.

I'm not a huge Splinter Cell fan, having played only Chaos Theory, but enjoy the occasional old fashioned stealth. I was originally put off of this fearing that it would follow trends into actionization, but bit the bullet when the game dropped under ten bucks and was pleasantly surprised.
It is indeed a stealth game still, just streamlined in some ways. For example, Chaos had noise and light meter telling you how obvious you were in relation to your surroundings, and you could modify your speed finely using the mouse wheel to crawl as slow as you want. In Blacklist, you just crouch-walk constantly for near silence and your gear glows when your fully shadowed.  This isn’t a bad thing; meter-based stealth is a little silly. Like any good stealth game, every area is still a puzzle and you have to figure out how to solve it with the tools you have. But at times I felt I would prefer a little more than just diving from cover to cover or climbing from place to place. Maybe something like Hitman's disguises and just a way of interacting with guards without fists would be interesting.
There are a couple levels that really feel they put stealth aside for combat. Typically they involve some story reason triggering the alarm and just flooding you with enemies, but near the end there’s two particularly annoying  first person segments following a secondary character. While you can still stealth these parts, it’s just aggravating to be placed in a totally different game without your normal equipment, and just frankly pointless, I gave up and went through them guns blazing. The more cynical side of me wants to think Ubi’s testing the water to see how much they could make this game a shooter. But as it stands, those segments are short and few.
There’s a good amount of customizations. You get the full suite of Splinter Cell tools, cameras, noisemakers, a particularly cheaty feeling drone, etc., that you have to conform to your limited inventory. There’s as always lethal and non-lethal options, with non-lethal stealth rewarding the most points which goes into upgrades for your armor, weapons, and goggles (one thing that made me a little sad is that I never really had to use the night vision goggles, and only used them for thermal). I never felt that my upgrades mattered too much because most of the time I was using melee takedowns, but I did enjoy being able to change the color of my stealth lights. It’s the little things, you know?
Plot wise its okay. Basically Echelon’s been at it again to stop some bad dudes with something called a blacklist, which I never really understood. There is a list that’s central to the game, but it’s not a blacklist. But eh, semantics. One thing that bothered me is that there were zero twists. There were developments, sure, but nothing felt unexpected, which you would expect in a Clancy/espionage type of story. Maybe it’s a meta twist.
Graphics are a hit and miss. Some areas felt like I was just looking at flat texture all over the walls, but other times you get nice vistas and well produced scenes.  Half of the character models had weirdly huge flat eyes despite the other half looking real sharp. While the preview videos showed a lot of your typical boring desert places, you actually go through quite a number of settings, each level had some nice unique character. Overall, it’s not a bad looking game by any means, but overall I felt it just missing some shaders or something. Even tried to add some with SweetFX, but didn’t work. Performance wise, generally 45-30 FPS at 1920x1200 Ultra on a GTX 760, with some random chugging but nothing distracting for the most part.
There is multiplayer, co-op, which looks very fun but haven’t had the chance to play, and Spy vs Merc, which is pretty dead, both with customizations like single player. I wouldn’t buy the game expecting to get hours out of them, but would recommend getting another copy to play through co-op with a like minded friend.
What I did like about the game was just the production values. Good cast of voice actors (with Adam Jensen as the closest this game had to a comedy relief character), very nice menu aesthetics, good soundtrack, and just an overall slick feeling. It’s hard to put to words, but the game just feels well made in a sense.
There’s a couple lingering issues. One is UPlay, which is an instant deal breaker for some. I had lots of start up issues throughout, starting but not recognizing keyboard, starting but minimized and not recognizing mouse, starting but playing the intro videos 10 pixels wide in the corner and not letting me skip…it was annoying, but nothing I couldn’t get past, and frankly, haven’t had with other Ubi games. Also, the game lacks a main menu, every boot up you either choose to resume last checkpoint or get to walk around your hub ship. This is particularly agitating the first time you play it, as you can’t access any options and will have wonky video settings until you get through a opening part.  All in all, it didn’t crash though, and wasn’t unbearable.
I realize I’ve had a lot of criticisms throughout this review. But I still liked the game. The core stuff, stealth, is still there and great. The game has a good amount of depth and a great length, 10 hour campaign on Realistic, considering a Perfectionist run, and a number of co-op missions which you can also solo. I really don’t think the issues I’ve had with the game are enough to really tarnish it, just hold it back from real greatness. If the stealth was just a bit deeper and the graphics a little sharper I’d jump onto the Splinter Cell boat. But for now, it’s just a good AAA stealth game, and that's fine by me.
